name: people_it
items: A 16-year-old vocational student in Taranto, Puglia, lives with his grandmother and uses voice typing because spelling makes him anxious.
A 17-year-old secondary-school student in Bellinzona, Ticino, plays clarinet in a youth wind band and is researching apprenticeships.
A 19-year-old hotel-management student in Rimini, Emilia-Romagna, works breakfast shifts on weekends and shares a flat with two classmates.
A 21-year-old unemployed woman in Carbonia, Sardinia, cares for her younger brother and relies on an older Android phone with limited data.
A 23-year-old dairy-farm worker in a village near Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige, helps manage the herd and follows mountain-bike repair videos.
A 25-year-old nursing student in Naples, Campania, commutes from a crowded family home and wants concise explanations of medical terminology.
A 27-year-old warehouse picker in Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna, works rotating night shifts and is preparing for the driving-licence theory exam.
A 29-year-old primary-school teacher in Perugia, Umbria, has recently adopted a child with her partner and enjoys designing low-cost classroom activities.
A 31-year-old fishing-boat mechanic on Lampedusa, Sicily, left school at sixteen and learns best from numbered, practical instructions.
A 33-year-old freelance translator in Lugano, Ticino, works in Italian, German and French and carefully checks differences between Swiss and Italian usage.
A 35-year-old home-care aide in La Spezia, Liguria, supports older clients, raises a daughter alone and often types requests between appointments.
A 37-year-old vineyard worker near Asti, Piedmont, is active in a local volunteer fire brigade and keeps handwritten weather records.
A 39-year-old municipal clerk in Matera, Basilicata, handles residency paperwork and is cautious about privacy when using unfamiliar digital tools.
A 41-year-old electrician in Mestre, Veneto, runs a two-person business and uses an AI assistant mainly to draft quotations and client messages.
A 43-year-old bookshop owner in Orvieto, Umbria, organizes readings for local schools and prefers technology that does not require coding.
A 45-year-old laboratory technician in Milan, Lombardy, co-parents two teenagers and spends weekends restoring an old touring bicycle.
A 47-year-old sheep farmer in inland Sardinia, lives in a multigenerational household and checks market information through a weak rural connection.
A 49-year-old bus driver in Turin, Piedmont, recently began studying family history and scans old parish documents after late shifts.
A 51-year-old social worker in Bologna, Emilia-Romagna, assists families facing eviction and wants neutral language for sensitive correspondence.
A 53-year-old supermarket cashier in Aosta, Aosta Valley, speaks Italian and French at work and is learning to manage household finances in spreadsheets.
A 55-year-old stonemason in Carrara, Tuscany, has decades of workshop experience but asks his son for help with online forms and attachments.
A 57-year-old public-hospital physiotherapist in Palermo, Sicily, cares for an elderly parent and enjoys growing herbs on a small balcony.
A 59-year-old owner of a seaside laundry in Senigallia, Marche, employs three seasonal workers and needs help understanding energy bills.
A 62-year-old postal worker nearing retirement in Cosenza, Calabria, sings in a community choir and is digitizing boxes of family photographs.
A 65-year-old recently retired civil engineer in Genoa, Liguria, lives alone, follows port redevelopment projects and is comfortable with technical software.
A 68-year-old former textile worker in Prato, Tuscany, helps with two grandchildren and uses a tablet mainly for recipes, video calls and health appointments.
A 72-year-old retired railway conductor in Chiasso, Ticino, volunteers at a local museum and likes comparing historical timetables.
A 76-year-old widowed olive grower near Lecce, Puglia, still manages a small grove and dictates messages because touchscreen keyboards frustrate him.
A 81-year-old retired pharmacist in Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, reads newspapers in several languages and wants sources clearly separated from opinions.
A 85-year-old former school caretaker in a village near Ragusa, Sicily, lives with his wife, makes wooden toys for great-grandchildren and uses a shared family laptop.
